texts.period: Sumerian King List tradition and Berossus, c. 290 BCE as preserved in George Smith 1876

source.work: The Chaldean Account of Genesis, ch. on Berossus and the antediluvian kings, George Smith (1876)

summary.en: Ten kings reigned before the flood, each for tens of sars — 432,000 years in Berossus' sum — the first at Eridu; then the flood swept them, and kingship began again from Kish: history framed between two descents of kingship from heaven.
summary.zh: 洪水前有十王，各在位數以萬年——貝羅蘇斯總計四十三萬二千年——首位建都埃利都；洪水掃盡其後，王權復自基什而始：歷史框於兩次王權天降之間。

sensitivity.note: Ancient chronicle tradition; no living community restrictions.

passages.text: Ten kings reigned before the flood, the first at Eridu, each for reigns counted in sars — 432,000 years in Berossus' sum — until the flood swept them away.
passages.note: Paraphrase of the antediluvian king list tradition as given by Berossus in George Smith (1876); not verbatim.

passages.text: After the flood kingship descended again, to Kish, and history ran between two descents of kingship from heaven — the frame that all Mesopotamian chronology kept.
passages.note: Paraphrase of the king list frame (Smith 1876; cf. Sumerian King List); not verbatim.

functions: Bridge between flood myth and dynastic history
Echo in the patriarchal ages of Genesis

variants.name: The Sumerian King List (ETCSL c.2.1.1)
variants.summary: The native list with eight antediluvian kings.

variants.name: Genesis 5 genealogies
variants.summary: The biblical echo of the antediluvian reigns.

primary_sources.work: Antediluvian king list (Berossus and the Sumerian King List tradition)

secondary_sources.work: Legends of Babylon and Egypt in Relation to Hebrew Tradition

region.zh: 波斯灣海岸（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Berossus' Babyloniaca, c. 290 BCE, preserved in George Smith 1876

source.work: The Chaldean Account of Genesis, ch. on Berossus, George Smith (1876)

summary.en: In the first year there came out of the Erythraean sea a monster named Oannes, the body of a fish with a man's head beneath — and he taught men letters, arts and the building of temples: the culture-hero of civilization rising from the sea.
summary.zh: 首年，海中出現名為俄安內斯的怪物：魚身而有人首，於魚腹之下——教人文字、技藝與建殿之法：文明源於滄海的文化英雄。

sensitivity.note: Hellenistic retelling; no living community restrictions.

passages.text: In the first year there came out of the Erythraean sea a monster named Oannes: the body of a fish, and beneath the fish's head a man's head, and a man's voice — the composite image of the wisdom from the deep.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Berossus' account of Oannes as given in George Smith (1876); not verbatim.

passages.text: He taught men letters, arts, laws and the building of temples, and at sunset he returned to the sea and passed the night in the deep — civilization's teacher rising daily from the water that had birthed the world.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Berossus' account (Smith 1876); not verbatim.

functions: Culture-hero myth of wisdom from the sea
Hellenistic dress of the Enki tradition

secondary_sources.citation: Donald A. Mackenzie, London, 1915, ch. on Oannes

title.en: The Sacred Marriage of the King

region.en: Temple bedchamber, Uruk and Isin, Iraq
region.zh: 烏魯克與伊辛神殿寢室（伊拉克）

texts.period: Uruk III to Isin I rites, c. 3000-1900 BCE (Jastrow 1898)

source.work: The Religion of Babylonia and Assyria, the Zagmuk symbolical marriage, Morris Jastrow (1898)

summary.en: On the New Year the king takes the place of the god and the priestess that of the goddess: the union performed in the temple bedchamber secures the year's abundance — the rite to which the love songs of Inanna and Dumuzi are the liturgy.
summary.zh: 新年之際，國王代神而立、祭司代女神而立：神殿寢室中的結合保障來年豐饒——伊南娜與杜穆茲情歌即此儀式之禮文。

sensitivity.note: Reconstruction of an ancient rite; presented as scholarly material, not endorsement.

passages.text: On the New Year the king takes the god's place and the priestess the goddess's: the union performed in the temple bedchamber secures the year's abundance.
passages.note: Paraphrase of the sacred marriage rite as reconstructed in Jastrow (1898); not verbatim.

passages.text: The love songs of Inanna and Dumuzi are the rite's liturgy: the bride-goddess claimed, the bed blessed with cedar oil, the city renewed by the annual performance.
passages.note: Paraphrase of the rite (Jastrow 1898); not verbatim.

functions: Annual fertility rite of king and goddess
Liturgical frame of the Dumuzid-Inanna love songs

variants.name: Iddin-Dagan A
variants.summary: The Isin dynasty's liturgy of the same rite.

variants.name: The wedding of Inanna and Dumuzid
variants.summary: The Uruk cult song of the rite.

secondary_sources.citation: Thorkild Jacobsen, New Haven, 1976, on the sacred marriage

region.en: Gates of the temple, Jerusalem echo (pin at Uruk)
region.zh: 神殿之門（定位於烏魯克）

source.work: The Religion of Babylonia and Assyria, the Tammuz wailing rites, Morris Jastrow (1898)

summary.en: In the month of Tammuz the women sit at the gate wailing for the shepherd below — the ritual lament that reached the Hebrew prophets' pages — the dying god mourned that the grain may rise.
summary.zh: 塔穆茲月，婦女坐於門前為冥下牧神哀哭——此儀式性哭喪直達希伯來先知的書頁——悼垂死之神，俾五穀得升。

sensitivity.note: Ancient ritual tradition; no living community restrictions.

passages.text: In the month of Tammuz the women sit at the gate wailing for the shepherd below — the ritual lament that reached the Hebrew prophets' pages.
passages.note: Paraphrase of the Tammuz wailing rites as discussed in Jastrow (1898); not verbatim.

passages.text: The mourning is functional: the dying god mourned that the grain may rise — the liturgical calendar's hinge of death and renewal.
passages.note: Paraphrase of the rites (Jastrow 1898); not verbatim.

functions: Cult practice of the dying-god myth
Ritual calendar hinge of death and renewal

variants.name: Dumuzid and Geshtin-ana
variants.summary: The narrative charter of the half-year.
